name: Letterly
tagline: Speak into your phone and get cleaned-up, reformatted text instead of a raw transcript.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The engine here is not secret: record audio, send it to a speech-to-text model, then ask an LLM to rewrite it as an email, a note, a summary, or a message. An agent can hand you a working local version of that loop in an evening, and on a laptop it will feel fine. The gap is everywhere the product actually lives: a mobile app, a share sheet, a system keyboard, background recording, sensible behavior when the phone locks or the network drops. Multi-language handling and the little style presets are also more tuning than they look. Build it for your desktop and you get most of the value; build it for your pocket and you are shipping an app, not a script.
coreLoopDIY: A local browser app that records your voice, transcribes it with a hosted speech model, rewrites it into a chosen style with an LLM, and puts the result on your clipboard.
requirements: An API key for a hosted transcription and chat model, or a local whisper.cpp build
A microphone and a machine you are willing to leave running
whatYouLose: Native iOS and Android apps, including the keyboard and share sheet that make dictation actually convenient
Reliable background and lock-screen recording on a phone
Tuned multi-language and code-switching behavior that mostly just works
Style presets someone else already tested against thousands of messy recordings
moatNotes: The moat is mobile ergonomics, not the model. Anyone can call a transcription endpoint; few can make it feel instant from a lock screen.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because dictation is a habit, and habits die on friction. Paying a few dollars a month means the button is always there, on the device you are already holding, with no key to rotate and no laptop to wake. A self-hosted version is genuinely useful for long-form drafting at a desk, but it will not replace the moment you are walking and want to dump three paragraphs into a note.
notes: Great desktop replacement, mediocre pocket replacement, which is unfortunately where the app is used.
prompt:
Build a local voice-to-formatted-text tool called "Dictly" in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20 with Express for the backend, plain TypeScript.
- A single static frontend page served by Express: vanilla HTML, CSS, and TypeScript compiled with esbuild. No React, no framework.
- No database. Store history as JSON lines in ./data/history.jsonl.

Frontend behavior:
- One big record button using MediaRecorder, capturing audio/webm.
- Show a live elapsed timer and a waveform-free simple level meter.
- On stop, POST the blob to /api/transcribe as multipart form data along with a selected style.
- Style selector with exactly these presets: Raw, Clean Note, Email, Message, Bullet Summary.
- Show the raw transcript and the rewritten text side by side, each with a copy button.
- Keep a scrollable list of the last 50 entries loaded from /api/history.

Backend behavior:
- POST /api/transcribe: accept the audio, send it to a hosted speech-to-text endpoint, then send the transcript plus a style-specific system prompt to a chat model, return both texts as JSON.
- Each style is a hardcoded system prompt in one file, styles.ts, easy to edit. Raw skips the rewrite entirely.
- Append every result to history.jsonl with timestamp, style, duration, raw text, rewritten text.
- GET /api/history returns the last 50 entries.
- Read API_KEY and API_BASE_URL from .env via process.env. Never hardcode secrets. Ship .env.example.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, mobile apps, cloud deploy, telemetry, payments, global hotkeys, audio file uploads from disk.

Deliverables: package.json with "npm run dev", README with three-step setup, working microphone permission handling, and a clear error banner when the API key is missing or a request fails.
